answers.answer: Behaviour change: the invitation report now adds a date to each row. The packet's scene 1 says: "This pull request adds a date to each row of the invitation report." and "It shows when the prospect was added." Scene 2 adds: "Before this change, the report row showed none of it." and "Now the report row carries that exact timestamp as date added." A matched prospect row supplies its creation time ("created_at"), or unknown when missing; bad values show as unknown. For whom: the reader/reviewer of that report sees the new date per row; the packet does not name any other user group.

The new helper _date_added in src/linkedin_mdp_mcp/invitation_shortlist.py. The packet shows it through the diff scene's call site, line 1031: row.update(_date_added(row["profile_url"], prospects, now)), plus its quoted lines 453 (if len(matches) != 1:) and 472-476; the helper's def line is not shown in the packet.

To reject a future timestamp the new code checks if parsed > now: (line 475) and records provenance["reason"] = "future_timestamp" (line 476). Other rejection paths shown: line 453 if len(matches) != 1: (not exactly one matching prospect row), and line 472 except (ShortlistInputError, OverflowError): which records provenance["reason"] = "invalid_timestamp" (line 473) and returns {"date_added": None, "date_added_source": provenance} (line 474). Scene 3 lists the cases: (None, "missing"), (42, "invalid_timestamp"), ("0001-01-01T00:00:00+01:00", "invalid_timestamp"), ("9999-12-31T23:59:59-01:00", "invalid_timestamp"), ("not-a-timestamp", "invalid_timestamp"), ("2026-09-30T14:12:13", "invalid_timestamp"), ("2026-10-03T00:00:00Z", "future_timestamp").

Supporting assertions from the receipts: row["date_added"] == created_at (L650), assert row["date_added"] is None (L710), assert str(created_at) not in json.dumps(row) (L716), and the case table at L693-699 ((None, "missing"), (42, "invalid_timestamp"), ("0001-01-01T00:00:00+01:00", "invalid_timestamp"), ("9999-12-31T23:59:59-01:00", "invalid_timestamp"), ("not-a-timestamp", "invalid_timestamp"), ("2026-09-30T14:12:13", "invalid_timestamp"), ("2026-10-03T00:00:00Z", "future_timestamp")), with created_at = "2026-09-30T14:12:13.123456+02:00" (L621).

The packet contains no separate 'start here' statement; its only code walkthrough is scene 4, 'The change, line for line', so that is where to start: src/linkedin_mdp_mcp/invitation_shortlist.py, first receipt line 453 (if len(matches) != 1:), then 472-476 (except (ShortlistInputError, OverflowError): / provenance["reason"] = "invalid_timestamp" / return {"date_added": None, "date_added_source": provenance} / if parsed > now: / provenance["reason"] = "future_timestamp"), then the call site 1030-1031 (for row in rows_out: / row.update(_date_added(row["profile_url"], prospects, now))). The behaviour tests to read next are in tests/e2e_invitation_shortlist.py at L669, L703 and L720.

False. Adding date_added only enriches each selected output row; the new tests pin that this date information cannot affect selection or eligibility: "An exact URL alias may enrich output, but its source time cannot affect selection." (tests/e2e_invitation_shortlist.py:669) and "A missing creation time is not inferred and cannot alter eligibility." (:720). The diff also applies the date after selection: for row in rows_out: row.update(_date_added(row["profile_url"], prospects, now)) (lines 1030-1031). The packet shows no membership or ranking effect.
